messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - gpu-pool-saturation detected for pool 'eu-west-1-gpu-a', queue depth growing for model=redwood-7b-qa; autoscaler failed to add nodes (scale cap hit). Paging oncall. thread_ts=5067894321
Jordan (oncall): I'm on it. seeing 99th latency spikes and token rate throttle. customers reporting timeouts. queue length ~4300 across frontend shards.
Mina (serving): paging logs show batch/kv-cache miss rate jumped ~8x starting 5067893600. suspect config rollout from yesterday: continuous_batch_window changed from 20ms -> 200ms and prefix_cache_ttl lowered.
Sanjay (runtime): autoscaler logs -> "scale_request_rejected: pool_cap_reached" across 3 regions. scale_limit for that customer tier is 10 instances, all consumed. also seeing k8s HPA events delayed due to API rate limit spikes.
Nora (ops): let's open a temporary quota bump with cloud team. I'll DM infra to request emergency burst +1 instance per pool. ETA ~10m.
Jordan (oncall): immediate mitigation options? reduce incoming concurrency or disable continuous batching to reduce KV cache pressure. we need to lower queue growth now.
Mina (serving): agree. disabling continuous batching will drop ideal batching efficiency but should reduce long tail stalls from prefix cache misses. patch: revert continuous_batch_window to 20ms and set prefix_cache_ttl back to 300s.
Ben R.: pushing revert now. deploying to canary in eu-west-1  -> running `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/serving PRODUCTION_BATCH_WINDOW=20` and `redwoodctl config set pool.eu-west-1.prefix_cache_ttl=300`
Deploy Bot: deploy started by Ben R. commit abc123 -> canary on 2 pods.
Mina (serving): also suggest transiently lowering per-pod max_concurrency from 32 -> 16 to reduce hot-shard saturation; will cut throughput per GPU but avoid queue blowups.
Jordan (oncall): Apply concurrency cap on serving config. Nora, coordinate rate-limit to clients that are sending spikes (support to inform top customers).
Nora (ops): rate-limit rule applied for anonymous/guest keys: 50rps global. Support Bot, can you open a customer-impact thread?
Support Bot: Created CS ticket #INC-6423 summarizing outages: degraded generation latency and occasional 502s for customers using redwood-7b-qa since ~13:40 UTC. Tier A customers: 4 impacted, Tier B: 12.
Sanjay (runtime): Autoscaler: I'm seeing backoff failures because the scale controller attempted +2 twice and hit pool quotas; cloud responded with error code QUOTA_EXCEEDED. That explains rejections.
Jordan (oncall): What's the expected time to see queue drain after revert + concurrency cap?
Mina (serving): should start to see improved batch hit rate within 30-60s of config rollout, KV cache rehits ramp in ~5m. but queue drain depends on total backlog; estimate 12-18m to get under 500 queue depth if no further spikes.
Ben R.: canary healthy, rolling to 20% -> 100% now. changes applied to eu-west-1.
Deploy Bot: rollout complete for env PRODUCTION_BATCH_WINDOW=20 on pool eu-west-1.
Jordan (oncall): queue depth now 3100 -> 2400 after first 2m. latency p95 coming down from 2.3s to 1.1s. good sign.
Nora (ops): cloud granted temporary soft-quota +2 instances for 30m. autoscaler has room to open 2 more nodes, but global cap still near-saturated.
Sanjay (runtime): I've increased autoscaler retry window and added one-off scale request to bump ephemeral nodes. instantiation in progress. logs show prefix_cache_miss_rate halving.
Jordan (oncall): customer impact update: Support Bot, please notify affected customers that we mitigated the surge, feature regression in batching config identified and reverted. we'll follow up with postmortem.
Support Bot: Notified customers with templated message. reference INC-6423.
Mina (serving): root cause preliminary: config rollout (change in continuous_batch_window + aggressive cache TTL change) increased KV cache churn and caused many small batches to miss cache prefetched keys -> more CPU on host, slower KV refills, which amplified queueing and pushed autoscaler to its limit.
Ben R.: leaving a TODO to pin batch window value in config defaults and add guardrail to prevent >100ms continuous_batch_window in production pools.
Jordan (oncall): Reopen incident if queue growth > 1000 after 30m or autoscaler rejects again. otherwise close and hand to postmortem. I'm switching to follow-up mode. :thumbsup:
pagerbot: Incident SEV2 acknowledged. Handoff to postmortem owner @Mina (serving). Next steps: create postmortem, include timeline, config diff, and customer impact.
Mina (serving): I'll own the postmortem. assigning due end of day tomorrow. will include runbook addition: when prefix_cache_miss_rate > 3% trigger automatic rollback of recent batching-related config changes.
Jordan (oncall): thanks all — great quick ops. I'll publish summary to #incidents-ops later.
Nora (ops): marking cloud burst release and auth escalation in ticket.
Support Bot: Ticket updated: customers informed, CS follow-ups scheduled.
Ben R.: quick note: captured the change diff from config service: `continuous_batch_window: 200` -> `20`, `prefix_cache_ttl: 60` -> `300`. adding to incident artifacts.
Mina (serving): final status at last_message_ts=5067894741: queue depth 420 (recovering), p95 0.95s, autoscaler healthy with +1 temporary node. moving to post-incident review. :white_check_mark:
